text: Including the coefficient-subcoalgebra-valued map back into C returns the original coefficient map. Corestriction changes only the codomain, so this equation follows from its defining inclusion identity. The finite free hypothesis supplies the coefficient subcoalgebra of [Milne 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); flatness of C supplies the inherited coaction, without asserting injectivity of the coefficient map. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L86), [range_matrixCoefficientHom_le](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L220).
Checks the original coefficient value.
Checks the range lies in the stated subcoalgebra.

The bundled comodule morphism associated to φ evaluates at m as the coefficient (φ⊗id)ρ(m), with scalar multiplication identifying R⊗C with C. This is precisely the coefficient convention in [Milne 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The equality unfolds the construction and requires neither a basis nor finite generation of M. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L78), [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160).
Checks the whole underlying linear map.
Checks counit evaluation recovers φ(m).

For finite free M, each coefficient map lands in its finitely generated coefficient subcoalgebra, so it corestricts to a morphism into that regular subcomodule. This realizes the coefficient construction in [Milne 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Over semirings, the explicit flatness of C means tensoring with C preserves injections, enabling the inherited coaction. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebraHom_apply_coe](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L210), [range_matrixCoefficientHom_le](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L220).
Checks inclusion recovers the original map.
Checks the required coefficient containment.

After extending scalars, applying the counit to a coefficient morphism recovers the extended functional φ. The proof extends ε∘cφ=φ and identifies A⊗R with A. This is the evaluation-at-identity mechanism of [Milne 9.1–2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); it holds for arbitrary commutative value semirings, with no freeness, finiteness or faithful-extension assumption. Checks pass: [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160), [baseChangeEvaluation_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L62).
Checks the original counit identity.
Checks the scalar-extended functional interpretation.

The coefficient map m↦(φ⊗id)ρ(m) is a morphism to the regular right comodule C. Coassociativity proves its compatibility with Δ, exactly the matrix-coefficient identity of [Milne 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), expressed without a basis. The source proves this over commutative semirings for arbitrary comodules, without requiring coefficient maps to be injective. Checks pass: [comul_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L57), [matrixCoefficientHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L86).
Checks colinearity in its explicit coefficient formula.
Checks the bundled map has the stated values.

For a regular subcomodule N, pairing n with the restricted counit recovers n as an element of C. Naturality reduces the calculation to applying ε to the first factor of Δ(n), the coalgebra counit identity in [EGNO 1.20.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Flatness supplies N’s induced coaction; no finite-generation hypothesis is needed. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_counit_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L194), [matrixCoefficient_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L182).
Checks the ambient regular-comodule counit calculation.
Checks restriction along the subcomodule inclusion.

Bialgebra multiplication x⊗y↦xy is a morphism from the tensor square of the regular right comodule to H. Multiplicativity of Δ proves compatibility with the diagonal coaction of [EGNO 1.21](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The coefficient algebra H may be noncommutative: the construction keeps the order xy and requires no flatness assumption. Checks pass: [regularMul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L169), [regularMul_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L158).
Checks the ordered product on pure tensors.
Checks the underlying multiplication map.

The morphism from the trivial comodule on R evaluates at r as its image under R→C, equivalently r·1. The source obtains this from the underlying algebra-linear map. This is the bialgebra unit used in [Milne 9.2(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); the domain carries the specified trivial coaction, rather than an arbitrary coaction on R. Checks pass: [trivialToRegular_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L102), [groupLikeToRegular_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L76).
Checks the underlying unit map.
Checks the general group-like evaluation formula.

Forgetting the comodule structure leaves the linear map r↦r·g. Its domain has the right coaction determined by g, matching the one-dimensional correspondence in [EGNO 1.22.13–14](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). Over a semiring, GroupLike explicitly stores Δ(g)=g⊗g and ε(g)=1; no unspecified nonzero-element condition replaces the counit law. Checks pass: [groupLikeToRegular_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L76), [matrixCoefficient_groupLike](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L205).
Checks the pointwise scalar-multiple formula.
Checks coefficients for the same group-like coaction.

Regular-comodule multiplication sends x⊗y to xy, in that order. The equation follows from the underlying linearized multiplication, while its morphism structure uses the diagonal right coaction of [EGNO 1.21](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). H need not be commutative, and the statement concerns the ambient regular comodule without any inherited-submodule flatness requirement. Checks pass: [regularMul_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L158), [mulHom_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L111).
Checks the complete underlying multiplication map.
Checks the same order after restricting to containing subcomodules.

The unit map R→C becomes a comodule morphism by choosing the group-like element 1 of a bialgebra. Its source carries the trivial right coaction r↦r⊗1. This is the unit morphism behind [Milne 9.2(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); the source proves colinearity from the group-like laws, allowing a noncommutative coefficient bialgebra. Checks pass: [trivialToRegular_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L110), [trivialToRegular_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L102).
Checks the actual unit-map values.
Checks the underlying algebra-linear map.

The underlying linear map of the trivial-to-regular morphism is exactly the algebra structure map R→C. Specializing r↦r·g at g=1 proves the equality, preserving the tensor-unit convention used in [Milne 9.2(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The displayed local comodule instance selects the trivial coaction on the domain R. Checks pass: [trivialToRegular_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L110), [groupLikeToRegular_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L68).
Checks the resulting value on each scalar.
Checks the general underlying map before specializing g=1.

A group-like element g defines a morphism from the rank-one comodule on R to the regular comodule by r↦r·g. Its coaction equation follows from Δ(g)=g⊗g. This matches [EGNO’s one-dimensional correspondence](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47); the native semiring definition also stores ε(g)=1, which supplies the domain’s counit law. Checks pass: [groupLikeToRegular_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L76), [groupLikeToRegular_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L68).
Checks the defining scalar-multiple value.
Checks the underlying linear map.

Assuming every element of H lies in a finite regular subcomodule, products from two finitely generated submodules lie in one such subcomodule. The multiplication image of their tensor product is finitely generated, so directed containment applies. This abstracts [Milne’s multiplication step](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); the resulting subcomodule need not be a subalgebra. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcomodule_of_fg_of_exists_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L241), [exists_finite_mul_le](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L154).
Checks containment of a finitely generated submodule under the stated covering hypothesis.
Checks the specialization where freeness supplies coverage.

When H is free over R, products from two finitely generated submodules fit inside a finitely generated regular subcomodule. A basis supplies finite-subcomodule coverage, extending [Milne 4.7–8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97), and the multiplication image is finitely generated. The initial submodules need not themselves be comodules, and no bialgebra compatibility is assumed here. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcomodule_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L141), [exists_finite_mul_le_of_exists_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L139).
Checks the free-coalgebra covering theorem.
Checks product containment from that coverage.

After including Q into H, the corestricted multiplication morphism sends n⊗p to np. The containment hypothesis ensures this product belongs to Q; Q need not be closed under all multiplication. This is the map used in [Milne’s multiplication argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), with flatness supplying the subtype coactions and the order of factors preserved. Checks pass: [mulHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L120), [regularMul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Regular.lean#L169).
Checks the underlying corestricted linear map.
Checks the ambient ordered product.

If Q contains every product np from N and P, it contains the multiplication image of every tensor in N⊗P. The source identifies that image with the product submodule, using the [tensor universal property](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). This is a linear containment statement: it requires no bialgebra compatibility or flatness of H. Checks pass: [mulHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L120), [mulHom_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L111).
Checks the containment used to corestrict the comodule multiplication map.
Checks the underlying multiplication formula in that specialization.

Multiplication corestricts to a comodule morphism N⊗P→Q when Q contains every product np. The source composes the inclusion maps with regular multiplication and proves containment on all tensors. This implements [Milne’s equivariant multiplication](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). Flatness of H supplies inherited coactions; neither commutativity of H nor multiplicative closure of Q is required. Checks pass: [mulHom_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L111), [mulHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L120).
Checks values after including Q into H.
Checks the complete corestricted multiplication map.

A coordinate in the scalar-extended basis equals evaluation against the scalar extension of the corresponding original coordinate functional. Tensor induction reduces the equation to a·map(bᵢ*(m)), matching [extension of scalars](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The given basis may have infinitely many indices: finite support of individual vectors suffices, without a finite-dimensionality assumption. Checks pass: [eq_of_baseChange_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L147), [baseChangeEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L68).
Checks these coordinate functionals separate all scalar-extended vectors.
Checks the scalar factor on pure tensors.

The functional represented by 1⊗φ is exactly φ extended to A⊗M. The universal lift evaluates its scalar coefficient at 1, giving the usual [extension-of-scalars formula](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). This identity holds for arbitrary modules over commutative semirings; it does not require the entire scalar-extended dual map to be an equivalence. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L68), [baseChangeEvaluation_one_tmul_baseChange](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L79).
Checks evaluation on arbitrary pure tensors.
Checks naturality under scalar-extended linear maps.

Evaluating the extended functional φ after the extended linear map f equals evaluating the extension of φ∘f. Tensor induction proves the identity from their equal values on pure tensors, as expected from [extension of scalars](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The statement concerns ordinary linear maps and needs neither finite generation nor faithfulness of R→A. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L68), [baseChangeEvaluation_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L62).
Checks the pure-tensor evaluation used in the proof.
Checks identification with the extended functional.

The pairing evaluates a⊗φ against b⊗m as ab·map(φ(m)). Both scalar coefficients therefore contribute, and the value lies in A. This is the bilinear [tensor-product evaluation](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV), proved by the scalar-extension lift formula. The source allows arbitrary modules over commutative semirings and does not assert a duality equivalence here. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L62), [baseChangeEvaluation_one_tmul_baseChange](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L79).
Checks the coefficient-one specialization.
Checks compatibility with linear maps.

For free M, equality against every extended R-linear functional forces equality in A⊗M. The proof chooses a basis and tests its coordinate functionals, the scalar-extended coordinate mechanism of [Milne 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). No finite basis or faithful extension is needed: it separates vectors already in A⊗M, rather than recovering vectors before base change. Checks pass: [baseChange_coord](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L126), [eq_of_baseChange_matrixCoefficientHom_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L179).
Checks extended dual coordinates are the new basis coordinates.
Checks the resulting coefficient-map separation used in reconstruction.

The canonical map A⊗M*→(A⊗M)* sends a⊗φ to the functional b⊗m↦ab·map(φ(m)). The source constructs it by the [extension-of-scalars universal property](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). It exists without finiteness assumptions; being an equivalence is a separate finite-projective result, so arbitrary scalar extension is not silently treated as commuting with duals. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L68), [baseChangeEvaluation_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L62).
Checks the full pure-tensor pairing.
Checks recovery of a single extended functional.

Compatible linear maps on a directed family glue on any submodule of its supremum. Directedness gives a common containing member, proving agreement and linearity, as in [Milne’s gluing argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). The source handles an empty indexing family by the zero map: then the supremum, and hence the domain, is zero. Checks pass: [iSupLift_mk](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Submodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L85), [iSupLift_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Submodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L130).
Checks every prescribed local value.
Checks uniqueness and independence of the chosen containing member.

For any real x and positive real y, some natural multiple n·y is at least x. Thus no real number is larger than every natural multiple of a fixed positive step. The multiplier is a natural number, not an arbitrary real; positivity of y is essential, since a zero step cannot reach positive x. Compared with [Kiming Theorem 3(1)](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L31).

The real numbers are linearly ordered: every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound, and every nonempty set bounded below has a greatest lower bound. These restrictions matter: this is conditional completeness, not a complete lattice. Lean separately assigns zero to the empty and unbounded cases where those extrema do not exist. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L136).

Real floor and ceiling return signed integers: floor(x) is the greatest integer ≤x, and ceiling(x) the least integer ≥x. They are not truncation toward zero; for example, floor(−1/2)=−1 while ceiling(−1/2)=0. The construction uses the Archimedean property to ensure integer bounds exist for every real input, including negative inputs. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L37).

The real infimum operation is defined by negating the supremum of the negated set. For a nonempty set bounded below, this gives its greatest lower bound. For an empty set or one unbounded below, Lean returns zero instead. That fallback makes the operation defined everywhere; it does not assert that zero is a lower bound. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L127).

The real supremum operation selects the least upper bound when the set is nonempty and bounded above. In every other case it returns zero. This is a deliberately total operation on sets of real numbers, not an extended-real supremum: an unbounded set receives zero rather than infinity, and zero need not bound its elements. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L115).

If a real-valued family has no lower bound, its indexed infimum in Lean equals zero. This records the chosen default outside the domain where a real greatest lower bound exists. For example, the family −n over natural numbers receives zero, even though zero is not a lower bound; the result does not represent negative infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L203).

The indexed supremum of a family whose every value is zero is zero, whether or not the index set has elements. For a nonempty family this is the ordinary supremum of the singleton {0}. For an empty family the same value comes from Lean’s separate empty-supremum convention, so no nonemptiness assumption is needed. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L178).

If every value of a real family is at most a, and a≥0, its indexed supremum is at most a. The nonnegative-bound condition handles an empty index set, whose supremum is defined as zero. Without that condition, an empty family and a=−1 would satisfy the elementwise bound vacuously but violate the conclusion. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L230).

A family of nonnegative real numbers has a nonnegative indexed supremum in Lean, even without assuming boundedness or a nonempty index set. In the ordinary nonempty bounded case this follows from the least-upper-bound property. The other cases also satisfy the inequality because the selected default is zero; no upper-bound property is asserted for unbounded families. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L295).

Applying a real-valued function that always has nonnegative outputs to any family produces an indexed supremum ≥0. Despite its name, NonnegHomClass requires only nonnegative outputs; it imposes no addition or multiplication law. The family may be empty or unbounded above, since Lean’s zero default for those suprema still makes the inequality true. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L297).

A real-valued family indexed by an empty type has indexed supremum zero in Lean. This is a default, not a claim that the empty subset of the reals has a least upper bound: every real number is an upper bound of that subset, and there is no least one. No family values are evaluated. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L174).

The infimum of the empty set of real numbers is defined as zero in Lean. Classically, that set has no greatest lower bound in the reals, because every real number is a lower bound. The theorem exposes a fallback making the infimum operation total; it is not an assertion that zero is the greatest such bound. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L189).

The infimum of the set of all real numbers is zero under Lean’s real-infimum convention. Since this set is unbounded below, it has no real greatest lower bound; in particular, zero is not a lower bound. The equation therefore describes the fallback chosen for an undefined classical infimum, rather than a statement about an actual extremum. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L171).

The supremum of the empty real set is defined as zero in Lean. Every real number is an upper bound of the empty set, so none is the least upper bound. This equation specifies a total-operation default outside the ordinary nonempty bounded setting; it should not be read as a mathematical extremum property of zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L168).

An input has integer ceiling z exactly when z−1<input≤z. The strict lower endpoint and inclusive upper endpoint are essential: integers round to themselves, while values just above z−1 round up to z. This characterization holds in any ring with a linear order and the stated floor/ceiling laws, not only for real inputs. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean#L667).

Taking the ceiling after including a signed integer z in the ambient ring returns exactly z, including when z is negative. The inclusion is exact arithmetic, not a floating-point approximation. The statement holds for any ring with a linear order and compatible floor/ceiling structure; no positivity assumption on the integer is needed. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean#L682).

Ceiling is nondecreasing: increasing an input cannot decrease its integer ceiling. This is weak monotonicity, not strict monotonicity; for example, the distinct real inputs 1/4 and 1/2 both have ceiling 1. The result uses only the ring, its linear order and its floor/ceiling laws, so it applies beyond the real numbers. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean#L659).

The integer floor of zero is exactly zero. Floor means the greatest integer not exceeding the input, so the boundary is inclusive: zero does not round down to −1. The result holds in any ring with a linear order and the stated floor structure and concerns signed integer floor, although natural-number floor agrees at this particular input. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean#L165).

The fractional part x−floor(x) is less than 1; together with the companion nonnegativity result, it lies in [0,1). This applies to negative inputs too: for real x=−1/2, floor(x)=−1 and the fractional part is 1/2. The theorem assumes the ring’s addition respects its linear order as well as the floor laws. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean#L445).

For a nonnegative input, taking natural-number floor and then including the result in the integers agrees with integer floor. The nonnegativity hypothesis matters: natural floor clips negative inputs to zero, while integer floor rounds downward; for real −1/2 the two results are 0 and −1. At zero both floors agree. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean#L949).

For a nondegenerate symmetric form of dimension 2m+1 over a finite field of odd cardinality q, this counts the full orthogonal group: 2q^{m²}∏_{i=1}^m(q^{2i}−1). Preserving matrices are automatically invertible. The finite range indexes i+1=1,…,m, and integer subtraction has its ordinary meaning; m=0 gives two elements. See [Cameron, Classical Groups, §6, pp.65–66](https://maths.qmul.ac.uk/~pjc/class_gps/cg.pdf). Checks pass: [invertibility](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/IsometryMatrices/Basic.lean#L145), [block count](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/IsometryMatrices/Field.lean#L156) and the [rank-one base](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/IsometryMatrices/FiniteField.lean#L169).
Every preserving matrix is invertible under the nondegeneracy hypothesis
Actual block orbit/stabilizer count underlying the order formula

For prime p and a symmetric nonsingular n×n matrix A over ℤₚ, this is the rational limit of counts of XᵀAX=A modulo pʳ, divided by p^{r·n(n−1)/2}. Eventual constancy ensures existence even at p=2. The normalization is twice GHS’s positive-rank density; outside the stated domain, the chosen limit has no specified mathematical value. See [Gritsenko–Hulek–Sankaran, §3.2, p.227](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/26000). Checks pass: [stabilization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/LocalDensity/Basic.lean#L541), [basis invariance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/LocalDensity/Basic.lean#L519), [positivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/LocalDensity/Basic.lean#L558), [rank-one family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/LocalDensity/Basic.lean#L647) and [hyperbolic p=3](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/LocalDensity/Basic.lean#L698).
The normalized count equals the density from 2v_p(2detA)+1 at every prime
Changing the integral p-adic basis preserves the density
